newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits steady to easier before CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits steady to easier before CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were steady to easier in thin trade with most traders sidelined before today's issue of the U.S. May consumer price index (CPI), housing starts and industrial production and capacity utilisation data, dealers said on Tuesday.
The consumer price index for May is forecast to show an increase of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.1 percent gain reported in April.
May housing starts is expected to be around 1.47 million annnualised units against April's 1.473 million units.
Industrial production for May is expected to show a gain of 0.2 percent from a 0.6 percent increase in April while May capacity utilisation is expected to be unchanged from April's 83.4 percent.

"Rates were generally steady this morning except for some light activity at the short end of the market. There's no fresh news but some people are waiting for today's issue of the consumer price index, housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilisation for fresh clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
In short dates, Tuesday/Wednesday and Wednesday/Thursday were unchanged from Monday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, respectively.
Week-fixed eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.

Among term rates, two-months eased 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, four-months was unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
